what: cut.py --start 1.5 --end 3 of an MXF (MPEG-2, GOP 12, 25 fps, start timecode 01:00:00:00) completed with source_carry.dropped ["timecode"]: the stream copy landed on the keyframe at 1.44 s and the output lost the start timecode that frame carries (01:00:01:11); cut.seek_keyframe read the keyframe at 0.96 s for the same -ss
escaped: the MXF case was recorded as a decision (a demuxer that lands on another keyframe than seek_keyframe reads) and the label withheld, so the drop was documented; no test compared seek_keyframe with the frame ffmpeg's -ss lands on for an MXF, and every fixture with a start timecode was an MP4/MOV, whose seek is by pts
mechanism: cut.seek_shift() returns 0 for a demuxer that seeks by pts (AVFMT_SEEK_TO_PTS) and DTS_HEURISTIC for the others; it listed MOV/MP4 only, but the MXF demuxer has the flag too, so seek_keyframe probed 3/23 s before where ffmpeg seeks and read the previous keyframe. seek_shift now names mxf with mov, first_frame_from no longer returns None for an MXF, and the label is written; test_a_stream_copy_cut_of_an_mxf_keeps_the_start_timecode_of_the_keyframe_it_lands_on pins the keyframe (1.44 s) and the written timecode (01:00:01:11)
